title: pigeonhole — S3 storage that keeps its bytes in chat messages
meta_desc: An educational storage system in Rust: an S3 gateway that cuts objects into chunks and posts them to Telegram and Discord channels, with a metadata log that lives there too.
hero.title: S3 storage that keeps its bytes in chat messages
hero.lede: pigeonhole speaks the S3 API, cuts objects into chunks and posts them as files to Telegram and Discord channels — or to a local disk. Its own metadata is a log of commands, and that log can live in a channel too.
replay.log_sub: one entry per change of state — click one to see its commands
replay.note: A real recording, not an animation drawn by hand: site/record.py ran the pigeonhole binary with JSON logs on and the AWS CLI against it, and this page plays the log back. The channels are fake Telegram and Discord channels in memory, the ones the demo runs on — the stores that post to them, and everything above, are the same code. The chunk size is lowered to 4 MiB so small files make several chunks (the default is 19 MiB). Played at human speed; the real time is next to each line.
js.say.CreateBucket: Bucket {bucket} created: no upload, one entry in the metadata log.
js.say.PutObject: {key} ({size}) became {chunks}, each posted to both channels; one log entry records the chunks and the object together.
js.say.PutObjectZ: {key} ({size}) became {chunks}: zstd shrank it to {stored} on the wire. Text compresses; random bytes do not.
js.say.CopyObject: {key} is a copy, and nothing was uploaded: the new object points at the same {chunks}, their refcount goes up. Only the log grows.
js.say.ls: The listing comes from memory: the state the log was replayed into. No channel is read.
js.say.end: That's it: the objects' chunks in two channels, and a log that can rebuild everything from scratch.
foot.warn: An educational project, not a file host. Using a messenger as general-purpose storage may break the Telegram and Discord terms of service; keep real runs to small test data in a private channel you own.
try.title: pigeonhole, running in your browser
try.lede: Not a recording. The server's Rust code — the metadata tablet on openraft, chunking and zstd, the replica group, the S3 handlers, and the Telegram and Discord stores themselves — is compiled to WebAssembly and runs in a Web Worker on this page. Only the services are fakes: in-memory channels that behave like Telegram and Discord. Nothing leaves your browser.
try.lede_plain: pigeonhole's Rust code compiled to WebAssembly, running in your browser.
try.note: Built from crates/web: the server's crates, read from the same pigeonhole.toml (below). Fake channels stand in for the services (fake = "memory", a build with the fake feature). Times are measured inside the worker.

js.say.DeleteObject: {key} is gone from the bucket. Its chunks are released; the posts stay until nothing points at them, then they are deleted.
js.say.repair: Repair: {n} missing copies written back from the others.
js.say.sweep: Sweeper pass: {n} posts that no chunk points to were deleted.

js.say.PutObjectInline: {key} ({size}) is small enough to live in the metadata log itself: no post in any channel ([inline] max_object_size).
js.say.PutObjectText: {key} ({size}) became {chunks} of {stored}: small enough for a text message, so the channels got text, not a file — 15 bits a character, as CJK ideographs.
js.say.restart: Restarted on the new config: the tablet claimed the log, loaded its snapshot and replayed {n} entries. The objects stay as they were; new ones follow the new rules.
js.try.erase_confirm: Erase the channels, the log and the objects kept in this browser? The demo starts over from the setup.
js.try.kept: Kept in this browser: a reload finds it all.

js.try.welcome_back: found your last visit's channels: {n} log entries replayed
js.say.welcome_back: Welcome back. Nothing here was kept by the page: the node booted from its channels on this browser's disk, claimed the log's next generation and replayed {n} entries — as a server does after a restart.

js.say.snapshot: The node took a snapshot of its state at position {at} and posted it to the snapshots channel. A boot now loads it and replays only what came after.
js.demo.post_barrier: generation {gen} confirms it holds the log (no entries)
js.demo.post_probe: a probe: where does the channel end
js.demo.log_note: An entry is one change of state; a post is a message in the channel. A batch post holds one or more entries; probes and claims are how the node finds the log's end and takes it over, so the counts differ. Entries before the snapshot are folded into it.
js.wiz.status: Set up your pigeonhole: nothing runs until you start it.
js.wiz.caption: Pick the channels, the copies, where the metadata lives and how fast the bots may post. The graph on the left follows your choices.
js.wiz.channels_lede: A file is cut into chunks, and each chunk becomes a message: a document, or text if it is small. Pick the channels the node posts them to.
js.wiz.copies_lede: With more copies a chunk survives a lost channel; with fewer, the channels share the work and hold more.
js.wiz.quorum: A write counts once this many copies are posted
js.wiz.quorum_note: {q} of {n}: the rest are posted in the background, and repair fills in a copy that failed.
js.wiz.one_channel: One channel: one copy of each chunk.
js.wiz.all_copies: Every chunk goes to all {n} channels.
js.wiz.all_shards: The {n} channels are shards: each chunk goes to one of them, the least busy.
js.wiz.mixed: {shards} shards of {copies} copies: each chunk goes to one shard, to every channel in it.
js.wiz.meta_lede: The node keeps its metadata (buckets, objects, where each chunk is) as a log of commands, posted to a channel of its own, and snapshots of it.
js.wiz.log_note: Every change is an entry. A restart reads the log back and is where it was.
js.wiz.toml_node_disk: The node's own disk (in the demo, this browser's storage): the log in log/, snapshots in snapshots/.
js.wiz.snapshots_off_node: The whole state as one file: a restart starts from it and replays only what came after. With the log in a channel, the snapshots are in one too: a node elsewhere must find both.
js.wiz.nodes_lede: One node, or a cluster of three. The nodes keep one metadata log between them by Raft: one leads and does all the work, the others follow, and one of them takes over when the leader is gone.
js.wiz.nodes_note_one: A single node: it leads itself.
js.wiz.nodes_note_many: Three nodes in this browser, as on three hosts: one leads, two follow; any two of them are a majority.
js.wiz.links_mixed_note: Nodes 1 and 2 directly, node 3 over the chat: its frames, and the others' to it, are posts in their outbox channels.
js.wiz.links_direct_note: Every node directly: gRPC between servers; in a browser, in memory.
js.wiz.links_chat_note: Every node over the chat: each posts its Raft frames to its own outbox channel and reads the others'. Slower, and the hosts need no network between them.
js.wiz.node_place_note: Node 1's are the metadata step's. Every node keeps its own log and snapshots; the chunks' channels are the same for all.
js.wiz.review_lede_many: One pigeonhole.toml for the cluster: every node runs it and finds its own log and snapshots in its [[node]] (on a server, PIGEONHOLE_NODE tells it which node it is). Start boots all three.
js.wiz.toml_cluster: A cluster of {n} nodes (Raft): this one file is every node's. The key comes from the environment; the outboxes are fake Telegram channels.
js.nodes.loft_sub: A node of the cluster: S3 in front, its copy of the metadata tablet (its own log and snapshots), the chunk store; only the leader writes.
js.nodes.looking: You look at node {n} now: its log, its channels, and your requests go to it.
js.nodes.following: You follow the leader: your requests go to whichever node leads (★).
js.nodes.new_leader: Node {n} leads now (term {term}): the others voted it in.
js.nodes.cut_note: Its links to the others go down, its outbox too. If it leads, the other two elect another in a few seconds; back, it catches up from the leader.
js.nodes.cut: Node {n} is cut off: nothing it sends gets through, and nothing reaches it.
js.nodes.back: Node {n} is back: it hears the leader again and catches up.
js.say.not_leader: Node {n} does not lead, so it turned the request away ({error}). Pick the ★ node, or follow the leader.
js.wiz.snapshots_note: The whole state as one file: a restart starts from it and replays only what came after.
js.wiz.every: A snapshot every so many entries
js.wiz.every_note: Fewer entries between snapshots: a faster restart, more snapshot posts.
js.wiz.bots_lede: A bot may post only so often to a channel. More bots on a channel, more posts a minute: each has a budget of its own.
js.wiz.bots_note: The node sends each call through the bot whose budget is ready soonest.
js.wiz.pace: How fast a bot may post
js.wiz.pace_real_note: Telegram lets a bot post about 20 messages a minute to a channel, Discord about 60. Uploads wait for their turn, as on a real server.
js.wiz.pace_demo_note: 20 posts a second per bot: nothing waits, so you see the rest of the system.
js.wiz.rate: {app}: up to {n} posts a minute per channel
js.wiz.review_lede: The setup as the config a server reads. Edit it if you like: the node parses it exactly as the binary does.
js.wiz.toml_data: Data channels: the chunks are messages here.
js.wiz.toml_copies: Every chunk on each of the {n} channels; a write counts after {q}.
js.wiz.toml_shards: {n} shards: each chunk goes to one of them.
js.wiz.toml_meta: The metadata log and its snapshots: two more channels.
js.wiz.toml_disk: Where the fake channels keep themselves: this browser's disk.
js.wiz.toml_fast: Faster than the services allow, for the demo.
js.wiz.toml_real: No [telegram.send] or [discord.send]: the services' own limits.

js.boot.log: {store}: the {app} channel of the metadata log.
js.boot.outbox: {store}: a node's outbox, its Raft frames to the others.

js.wiz.toml_lease: A Discord log is held by a lease (45 s on a server). A reload stops the node as a crash would, and the next start waits the lease out: short here.

js.demo.boot_failed: The node could not start on what this browser keeps (the error is above).
js.demo.fault_note: Break it: take the channel down, or clear it as an admin might. Reads go to another copy; a check finds what is gone, and repair puts it back.
js.demo.fault_down_note: The channel is down: every call to it fails. An upload whose write quorum needs this copy fails; with a smaller quorum it counts, and repair adds this copy once the channel is back.
js.say.down: {store} is down: every call to it fails.
js.say.up: {store} is back. Repair adds the copies it missed.
js.say.wiped: {store} lost its {n} messages, and the node does not know: reads go to another copy. Check the channel to find what is gone.
js.say.verified: Checked {checked} copies in {store}: {gone} gone, queued for repair.
js.say.failed_down: The upload failed: a channel is down, and the write quorum needs its copy. {error}
js.wiz.toml_repair: Repair passes in the background, as on a server (there every 30 s).

js.demo.bg_repair.one: Repair: {n} copy queued, the next pass in {s} s
js.demo.bg_repair.other: Repair: {n} copies queued, the next pass in {s} s

js.demo.bg_snapshot: Snapshot: {n} entries to go (the last at {at})
js.say.deleted_one: A message of {store} is deleted ({name}). The node finds out when it reads that copy, or when you check the channel.

js.say.repair_pass.one: A background repair pass wrote back {n} copy.
js.say.repair_pass.other: A background repair pass wrote back {n} copies.

js.say.read_failed_down: The read failed: one copy is down, and the other is gone. The read queued the lost one for repair. {error}
js.demo.group_meta: Metadata: the log and its snapshots
js.bg.parked: off: parked until turned on or run by hand
js.bg.entries: {n} of {of} entries since the last snapshot (at {at}): at {of} the tablet takes one
js.bg.idle: The last pass found nothing to do.
js.bg.asked: Asked the {task} for a pass now.
js.bg.turned_on: The {task} is on: {key} back on, an entry in the log.
js.bg.turned_off: The {task} is off: {key} = off, an entry in the log; it survives a restart.
js.bg.repair_note: Copies back what a read or a check found missing, from the other copies. A pass looks at the metadata only; it calls the channels just to copy.
js.bg.sweep_note: Deletes the posts no chunk uses: chunks no object needs any more, and orphans of failed uploads. A pass finds them in the metadata; it calls the channels just to delete.
js.bg.cool_note: Moves small objects kept in the log itself (inline) out to chunks once they go cold. A pass looks at the metadata only.
js.bg.snapshot_note: Writes the whole state as one file, so that a restart replays only what came after: every so many entries, and by time if that is on.
js.demo.owner_marker: Owner marker: this channel belongs to deployment {owner}; another deployment refuses it.
